I am 66 years old and I never went to school. I learned farming from my father and from watching my neighbors. I have 14.5 mu of land in Quzhou, me and my wife work it. We plant wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as everyone here. I always start from what I did last year — change is risky.

For wheat, after the maize comes off in October, I plough the field deep. I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — 50 jin bags, the 15-15-15 kind from the shop in the village. I sow the improved wheat seed, same as last year. In spring, when the wheat turns green, I spread half a bag of urea per mu, that is 25 jin. I irrigate three times: green-up, jointing, and filling. I spray twice, once for weeds and once for bugs. Last year I got 450 kg per mu, I hope for the same.

For maize, after wheat harvest in June, I rotary till quick because the season is short. I plant hybrid maize seed, the kind everyone buys, the red bag from the seed shop. I put down 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the row when planting, and when the corn is knee-high I spread 25 jin of urea per mu and hoe it in. I irrigate twice, three times only if it is very dry. Two sprays: herbicide at planting, insecticide later. I expect 550 kg per mu.

I do not trust new ideas. If the dealer pushes some new fertilizer, I wait to see if my neighbor uses it and gets more yield. Last year cost me enough already — compound fertilizer went up. But I would rather put a little too much than too little. A bad harvest means I lose everything; wasting a few jin of fertilizer is just money spent. I watch my costs, but yield comes first.
